problem: DRL navigation policies generalize poorly across speed limits, sensor/pose noise and scene layouts, and hinder sim-to-real transfer. Domain randomization corrupts the state distribution and makes exploration harder, so it can yield sub-optimal policies.
motivation: Training robots in the real world is expensive and zero-shot transfer can be dangerous, so robust generalization matters. Pose estimation error corrupts the egocentric map, while multi-modal inputs (laser + map) are complementary and can be used to recover the clean signal. A teacher trained in a noise-free environment can supply both a clean representation and a near-perfect policy for a student to imitate.
key_idea: Train a noise-free RL teacher with a contrastive auxiliary loss on egocentric maps, then distill a student that fuses noisy map and laser inputs by regressing the teacher's feature and matching its policy.
insight: The choice of representation space is essential. Removing the teacher's contrastive objective drops success from 81.2% to 56.1% even though the teacher still solves the ideal environment, so a good teacher policy alone does not make a good teacher. Removing feature distillation drops success to 72.5%. Laser input raises feature alignment (cosine similarity above 0.6 vs about 0.4 with the map alone). t-SNE shows the transform layer moves noisy features into the neighborhood of the clean label features.
method: Teacher: PPO agent with a 3-layer CNN on the noise-free egocentric occupancy map and a 2-layer FC on the laser; concatenated features feed the actor-critic. Dense reward: step -0.01, collision -0.05, goal +4.0, plus change in distance to goal.

Contrastive objective: InfoNCE (tau=0.25, beta=0.2) on two augmentations (ColorJitter, RandomScale) of the same map as positives and other batch items as negatives, with a MoCo-style EMA momentum encoder, so features are sensitive to relative pose information.
Student cross-modal fusion: CNN on the noisy map and FC on the noisy laser, followed by a 2-layer FC transform module T that predicts the teacher's clean map feature z_t.
Feature distillation: negative cosine similarity between z_t and T(z_hat, q_hat), using paired noisy/clean observations collected in simulation.
Policy distillation: KL(teacher policy || student policy); the total student loss is 0.25*FD + 0.75*PD, trained with supervised learning for 1M steps.
Task setup: a 2D simulated arena where the robot visits 5 randomly placed goals in order, with continuous velocity commands (vx, vy, omega).

setting.backbone: Small CNN (3 layers) + FC (2 layers) actor-critic teacher trained with PPO; student with CNN/FC fusion + transform FC, trained from scratch by distillation
setting.training_data: Trained from scratch in one 8.08m x 4.48m simulated environment: teacher 2M PPO steps with 4 parallel environments, student 1M steps with 2 parallel environments; no extra or web data
setting.observation: 2D laser scan (60 rays, -135 to 135 degrees) plus a 2.56m x 2.56m egocentric occupancy map cropped at the estimated pose, plus goal coordinates
setting.simulator: custom 2D simulator; real-world tests on a DJI RoboMaster EP with RPLiDAR S2
setting.privileged: Teacher uses the noise-free label map; the pre-built global occupancy map is assumed; real-robot pose comes from point-cloud matching against an existing map. The student uses no privileged information at test time.

numbers_note: No standard benchmark; all results are on the authors' own 2D multi-goal simulation. The real-robot experiment is qualitative only (figure and video), with no numbers.
results: CMFD beats the baselines (Pose+Laser, Map+Laser, Teacher) across speed, noise and scene shifts. Under the hardest noise it reaches 81.2% success vs 64.7% for Map+Laser (+16.5 points) with about half the collision time, and it reaches 80.2% on an unseen scene vs 72.2%. The real-robot run reaches all 5 goals qualitatively.
limitations: Evaluated only in a small custom 2D environment with a single training scene and no standard benchmarks; real-world results are qualitative only
Assumes a pre-built global occupancy map and no dynamic obstacles; focuses only on pose estimation noise
Fusion uses simple FC layers and needs paired noisy/clean observations available only in simulation
